eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service and AccuWeather forecasts projected Atlanta’s official high near 97–99 °F on August 17 under a persistent subtropical ridge favoring clear skies, strong solar heating, and light winds. This setup, well above the 88–90 °F August climatological normal at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, drove near-certain trader consensus on the 98–99 °F bin. Recent consecutive days reaching 96–98 °F reinforced the pattern, while modest ensemble spread limited upside beyond 101 °F. Any late-day convection remained the main variable that could have trimmed the peak, yet model consensus and station-specific resolution criteria supported the dominant positioning. New observational data from the official KATL station will finalize the outcome.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent influence from the North Pacific High is sustaining warm, humid southerly flow over the Korean Peninsula, supporting daytime maxima near the seasonal average for Busan in mid-to-late August.** Korea Meteorological Administration short-range guidance and supporting models indicate a forecast high around 30–33°C for August 18, with mostly cloudy morning conditions giving way to clearer skies and only low (10–20%) precipitation chances. Coastal sea breezes and marine air moderation, common along Busan’s shoreline, are expected to limit afternoon peaks and introduce the main source of uncertainty around exact maxima.

Recent model consensus shows limited day-to-day shifts, keeping the distribution tightly clustered. Historical climatology reinforces this: typical August highs in Busan range 29–31°C, with occasional convective activity or variable cloud cover preventing outliers. The market’s concentration on 29–31°C (combined ~86% implied probability) reflects traders’ assessment that these moderating factors—marine influence, possible isolated showers, and standard late-summer steering patterns—will keep the official daily maximum (measured at the primary KMA station) within that narrow band rather than allowing extremes above 32°C or below 28°C. Official observations the following day will resolve the market based on the verified peak reading.

Lower-probability tails for 18 °C or below acknowledge minor risks from localized cooling or measurement-site variations, while negligible odds above 23 °C align with the absence of anomalous heat signals in the latest official data. Traders weight these forecasts heavily because resolution depends on verified observations, typically from Helsinki-Vantaa Airport, where model consensus has historically proved reliable this time of year.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from PAGASA and other models indicate Manila's maximum temperature on August 18 will likely peak near 28–29°C under the influence of the southwest monsoon, which is delivering widespread cloud cover, heavy rainfall, and suppressed daytime heating across the region. These conditions align closely with the market's leading 28°C outcome at 45% implied probability, as persistent moisture and reduced solar radiation limit intensification beyond typical August baselines of 30–31°C. Cooler scenarios gain traction from ongoing rain bands, while probabilities for 30°C or higher remain low absent a rapid monsoon break or clearer skies in the final hours. Updated agency briefings on storm positioning and local observations will refine these trader-assessed odds ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) flow and associated cloud cover plus rainfall are the dominant factors capping Manila’s maximum temperature on August 19, 2026, near the historical August mean of ~30–31 °C.** Official PAGASA outlooks issued for the period project a daily high of 31 °C (with a 60 % chance of rain) under the influence of the monsoon and a distant low-pressure area east of northern Luzon; these conditions favor widespread cloudiness that limits solar heating and promotes evaporative cooling from frequent showers. Recent surface analyses and extended forecasts from multiple sources consistently show daily maxima in the narrow 28–31 °C envelope, consistent with climatology tempered by the active monsoon regime that has already produced moderate-to-heavy rains across Metro Manila in the preceding days.

Trader consensus reflected in the market probabilities—29 °C (38.5 %), 28 °C (23.0 %), and 30 °C (19.5 %)—aligns with this narrow range: the leading 29 °C outcome sits at the lower end of the forecast envelope where monsoon-enhanced cloudiness and precipitation are most probable, while the lower probabilities assigned to 31 °C or higher reflect the reduced likelihood of clearing skies or stronger insolation. Key near-term variables that could shift these implied odds include the next PAGASA model runs and any intensification or weakening of the monsoon trough; resolution will be determined by the official daily maximum recorded at the designated Manila observing station.
